doc.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: High school gigs at Lu and Charlie's with Ellis Marsalis; meeting Cannonball
summary: He played at Lu and Charlie's with Ellis Marsalis, Alvin Batiste and James Black, and met Cannonball Adderley in junior high.

venues.name: New Orleans Center for Creative Arts

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Before you left for Eastman, we’ll get to that in a minute, but was there enough work for you as a musician in New Orleans?

Yeah it was weird. I mean when I was in high school I was performing with Ellis Marsalis at a club, you probably are familiar, called Lu and Charlie’s. I don’t know if you’re familiar with Lu and Charlie’s?

Oh well let me mention this in the archive for you. Lu and Charlie’s was a very interesting venue. It was a club. It was owned by, oh my good friend, now Charlie Bering, who passed away maybe about six years ago. And Charlie was actually one of the producers of the Jazz and Heritage Festival but he had a club when I was in high school. And people like Alvin Batiste performed there, Ellis Marsalis performed there, all of the local New Orleans jazz giants performed there. And that was my first baptism into jazz and playing, like can you imagine being in high school and playing with Ellis Marsalis

and people like James Black on drums and all these wonderful musicians. I mean I was like in heaven, I was like a child in a candy shop. You know, like studying with Ellis during the daytime and performing with people like Alvin Batiste, I was still at that time performing with my father and you know they were bringing other musicians who love New Orleans, like Cannonball Adderley —

So I met Cannonball when I was in junior high. Man he was, you know, just so down to earth. Sometimes you have these expectations of like when you think about somebody like Cannonball, like a God you know. But you meet him and he’s just as genuine as his music was. And that’s the thing that really impressed me about a lot of the musicians who I met.
